extensions.paletteNote: Signal Room. Night: broadcast black #1A1A1A, metal #D2D4E1 and #EDEDED, signal blue #698BD3 (reference #3366CC lifted 34% toward metal; raw blue is 3.24:1 on black), lamp red #FF3036, cursor gold #E0AF46. Day: cream #E3CFAA, burgundy #5E292F for secondary text, paper inks #2D54A1, #962B31, #5F4E29. Hazard orange #F55B1D is a lamp-ramp step, not a fourth ink. Panels, borders, dim text, and meter-off are derived tints.

narrative.overview:
The site is a code buffer at stage scale. Source enters, findings come out, and the score sits on a master meter. The six families are listed once, under the floor. Nothing is dressed as a marketing page: the file tab, line numbers, syntax colour, cursor, and meter are the page's actual parts, and they keep working as navigation, copy controls, and reading structure.

The system is flat, square, and high-contrast. Broadcast black is the room. Exactly three inks carry meaning — signal blue for health and primary action, lamp red for strings, active state, and errors, cursor gold for warnings and the cursor. Running prose switches to a workhorse sans so the Read surfaces stay comfortable; code, numbers, and labels stay monospaced because they are code, numbers, and labels, not costume.

The light theme is the same buffer on cream paper: black ink, burgundy for secondary text, the same three hues darkened for contrast, while code and instrument panels stay on the night palette.
keyCharacteristics: Broadcast-black ground with hairline rules and square panels.
Three functional inks: signal blue, lamp red, cursor gold. No gradients, no glow halos.
Monospace for stage lines and measurements; Public Sans for long reading.
The hero is a working code buffer plus a score meter, not a headline over a screenshot.
Angie appears only on the 404, as a stage character.

rules.name: The Three Inks Rule
rules.body: Signal blue, lamp red, and cursor gold are the only chromatic inks. Hazard orange stays inside the lamp ramp. Neutrals, borders, and dim text are derived tints. A fourth hue is a bug.

rules.name: The No Glow Rule
rules.body: Nothing glows. Emphasis comes from solid fill, a hard 1px rule, or a scale step.

rules.name: The House Lights Rule
rules.body: Light mode is not an inversion. It is cream paper. Code and instrument panels stay on the night palette.

rules.name: The Mono-For-Data Rule
rules.body: Monospace is used for code, commands, counts, scores, line numbers, and labels. It never sets a paragraph of prose.

rules.name: The One Display Rule
rules.body: Only the landing headline uses the display step. Docs titles step down to the headline size.

rules.name: The Border-Not-Shadow Rule
rules.body: If a surface needs separation, add a 1px hairline or move it one tonal step. Do not add a shadow.

dos: Do keep exactly three chromatic inks and derive every other surface from the reference metal, black, burgundy, and cream. Borders, dim text, and meter-off are tints, not new hues.
Do use JetBrains Mono for code, commands, counts, and labels, and Public Sans for running prose.
Do put the score and the command in the first desktop viewport. State each sample number once.
Do keep docs prose near 40rem and align header, quickstart, pager, and prose to it.
Do preserve the pre-release status: build-from-source is the primary action, the npx command is labelled preview.
Do confine Angie to the 404 and keep the rest of the site mascot-free.
donts: Don't add gradients, glow shadows, glass, blurred panels, or colored halos.
Don't use radii above 2px on controls or any rounded cards.
Don't use monospace for paragraphs or sans for code.
Don't put an eyebrow or kicker above a heading; the buffer tab and line numbers are chrome, not labels.
Don't introduce a fourth accent for a new feature; give the feature a job inside the three inks.
Don't let the light theme invert code panels; instruments stay dark.
